subject: Error Bar not showing because the end of the bar is off the axis scale

messages.author: 10bdf5cd33ee419a
messages.subject: Error Bar not showing because the end of the bar is off the axis scale
parts:
I'm having problems getting an error bar to show bacause the end of
the error bar extends off the axis scale. If I increase the scale it
shows up but I want to be able to 'zoom' in on a specific dataset
section.

Here's some code that will reproduce the problem for you:

library (ggplot2)
upper.ci = c(2,6,8,10,12,20)
lower.ci = c(0.5,1.0,1.2,3,4,5)
est = c(1,2,3,5,6,7)
output = data.frame (cbind(est,upper.ci, lower.ci))
output$labels =c("R1","R2","R3","R4","R5","R6")

limits = aes (xmax = output$upper.ci, xmin = output$lower.ci)

myPlot = ggplot(data = output, aes( x=est, y=labels) )
myPlot = myPlot + scale_x_continuous (limits = c(0,10), name = "Odds
Ratio of Reaction") # if you comment out this line the error bars on
R5 and R6 will re-appear.
myPlot = myPlot + geom_point() + geom_errorbarh(limits, height=0.4)

Here are my example using my real data:
This is the example of the TumourGpB loosing its line because its got
a value of 30 which is off scale. In my view the line should extend
to 10 and then possibly have some means to indicate it is off scale
(eg dotted or and arrow)
http://php5.chemo.org.uk/MissingLine.png

This is the example of my data without the x axis being limited -
notice that TumourGpB is showing an error bar again, but that the
detail of the graph is lost because of the size of the error.
http://php5.chemo.org.uk/Line.png

Many thanks to someone for your help!

Calum

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Error Bar not showing because the end of the bar is off the axis scale
parts:
Hi,
There are two ways of limiting the range of a graph. Setting limits on
the scale discards data that falls outside those limits. Setting
limits on the coordinateness "zooms in" on a particular area of the
plot. So, get rid of the xlim settings in scale_x_continuous and set
them in coord_cartesian e.g., myPlot + coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,10))

Best,
Ista
